result.keywords: This fictional article examines a marginalized genre of ambulatory sound installations that blend acoustic ecology, portable sculpture, and nocturnal performance practice. It proposes a framework for analyzing tide-responsive resonators, hand-built listening chambers, and drifting public interventions, emphasizing aesthetic migration rather than robotic control, biomedical sensing, or image segmentation. Case studies focus on small-scale experimental ensembles operating in harbor districts, desert festivals, and temporary museums, with attention to spatial notation, resonant materials, and audience circulation.
result.title: Aurora of Glass Tides in Nomadic Soundfields.
